intake.title: Update the transitive AndroidX Fragment dependency flagged by Google Play
intake.body:
Google Play Console flags `androidx.fragment:fragment:1.1.0` under **Technical quality** for release **5 (0.1.2)**. The SDK publisher recommends **1.2.1 or later** before publishing the next app update.

Gradle confirms that the current release still resolves `1.1.0` transitively. One path is `review-ktx:2.0.2` → `play-services-basement:18.4.0` → `fragment:1.1.0`. Firebase Analytics also reaches Fragment through Google Play services. Update the release dependency graph to use a compatible stable Fragment version that meets the publisher’s minimum.

### Acceptance checks

- [ ] Run the command below and record the selected version. Every path in `releaseRuntimeClasspath` must resolve to `1.2.1` or later.
- [ ] Build the release AAB and pass the existing JVM and Android device suites, including the round-pairing review tests.
- [ ] After Play processes the next release, confirm that its SDK report no longer flags Fragment `1.1.0`.

```sh
./gradlew :app:dependencyInsight --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath --dependency androidx.fragment:fragment
```

[AndroidX Fragment release notes](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/fragment)

acceptance: Running `./gradlew :app:dependencyInsight --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath --dependency androidx.fragment:fragment` for the release variant reports a selected `androidx.fragment:fragment` version of `1.2.1` or newer, with no remaining `releaseRuntimeClasspath` path selecting `1.1.0`.
The next release AAB builds successfully and the existing JVM and Android device test suites pass, including the round-pairing review instrumentation tests in `RoundReviewTest`.
After uploading the next release and once Google Play finishes processing it, the Play Console SDK report for that release no longer flags `androidx.fragment:fragment:1.1.0` under Technical quality.
checks: Dependency verification: run `./gradlew :app:dependencyInsight --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath --dependency androidx.fragment:fragment` and record the selected Fragment version and the contributing dependency paths.
Release artifact verification: run `./gradlew :app:bundleRelease` to confirm the release AAB still builds with the updated dependency graph.
JVM regression suite: run the existing unit tests, at minimum `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`, to confirm no regressions in pairing, review-attempt storage, and related logic.

Android device regression suite: run the existing instrumentation tests, at minimum `./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest`, and confirm the round-pairing review scenarios in `app/src/androidTest/java/com/chunkymonkey/chess/tournament/review/RoundReviewTest.kt` still pass.
Post-release validation: after the next build is uploaded to Play, re-check the processed SDK report in Play Console and verify the Fragment 1.1.0 warning is gone for that release.
plan.release_notes: Updated app dependencies so release builds no longer include the outdated AndroidX Fragment 1.1.0 version flagged by Google Play.

findings: The verification note records nine passing RoundReviewTest cases, but it does not establish that the full Android device suite passed. Run `./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` and attach the report with the device API level, total test count, failures, and skips.
The Play Console acceptance check remains open. Once Google Play processes the next release, record the version code and confirm that its Technical quality report no longer flags Fragment 1.1.0.

The Gradle constraint is a reasonable way to upgrade the transitive dependency, and the note reports selection of Fragment 1.8.9, a successful release AAB build, and 25 passing JVM tests. This review had access only to the supplied diff and notes. Attach the actual release dependency insight output and build and JVM test results so those claims can be independently verified.
